text:
maya: heads up — main is red after i regenerated poetry.lock to pick up security transitive updates. failing integration test: tests/integration/storage/test_upload.py::test_multipart_upload. CI log shows OSError: [Errno 22] Invalid argument when boto3/s3transfer tries to seek a stream.

sam: yikes. can you paste the failing stack? and CI link?

maya: here —
```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/opt/hostedtoolcache/Python/3.10.*/x64/lib/python3.10/site-packages/s3transfer/upload.py", line 412, in _multipart_upload
    fileobj.seek(0, os.SEEK_END)
OSError: [Errno 22] Invalid argument
During handling of the above exception, another exception occurred:
  File "/workspace/project/tests/integration/storage/test_upload.py", line 78, in test_multipart_upload
    client.upload_fileobj(fileobj, Bucket=bucket, Key=key)
  ...
```

ci-bot: build: https://ci.example.com/builds/1970012210 (failed) :x: 

alec: i can reproduce locally with tox -e integration. looks like s3transfer changed behavior in 0.6.x — it tries to seek to the end to compute size which breaks non-seekable streams (we pass an io.BufferedReader wrapped around an aio stream in the test).

jen: did the lock bump actually update s3transfer? can you grep the lockfile?

maya: yes — poetry.lock shows s3transfer 0.5.1 -> 0.6.1 as part of botocore/boto3 transitive bump in the merge. my bad for not catching it in the PR.

ravi: quick options: pin s3transfer to 0.5.* in pyproject (constraint), revert the lock bump, or update our tests/impl to use a seekable tempfile for the integration test.

sophie: can someone run a quick bisect in CI: install s3transfer==0.5.1 in the environment and rerun the failing test? that should confirm the regression. happy to trigger a job.

sam: +1 do that in a branch so main stays green.

sophie: i kicked off a cron job in a branch installing s3transfer==0.5.1 then `tox -e integration -- tests/integration/storage/test_upload.py::test_multipart_upload`. it passed.

maya: thanks. i opened a small PR that adds a temporary constraint in pyproject.toml and regenerates the lockfile (link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/project/pull/482). also added a note in the PR body explaining the regression and linking the CI run.

jen: let's pin for now and file a follow-up to track upstream s3transfer change. also add a test tweak to use SpooledTemporaryFile (seekable) in the integration harness so we don't rely on non-seekable streams.

alec: agreed. i'll add the test change in a follow-up — keeps the integration closer to real-world but avoids the break.

maya: thanks everyone. will merge the pin PR once CI is green and open a ticket to follow upstream behavior. good catch @sophie and @alec :thumbsup:

sophie: np — leaving a comment on the PR with the bisect steps and logs.

maya: will follow up tomorrow with the incident ticket and retro notes.
